key_findings.detail:
Glass surface resistance is the dominant lateral leakage current pathway. Humidity exponentially reduces this resistance:

- A realistic diurnal humidity cycle (20°C/100% RH at night → 40°C/31.2% RH at midday) reduces glass surface conductivity by a factor of **63**
- **Glass surface resistivity activation energy:** 99 ± 14 kJ/mol with strong relative-humidity dependence
- [[papers/Wiley-136-1282-2-s2.0-85148423463-2023-J-Electrochemical mechanisms of leakage-current in photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=1|Vogt et al. (2023), p.1]]

Wet module conditions increase leakage current by approximately **35×** compared to dry conditions:
- [[papers/IEEE-171-2371-2-s2.0-85099585463-2020-C-Modeling of Leakage Currents in c-Si PV Modules and Investigation of their Arrhenius Behavior.pdf#page=2|Spataru et al. (2020), p.2]]

Water ingress raises the conductivity of EVA encapsulant by orders of magnitude:

- Dry EVA specific resistance: ~$10^6$–$10^7$ Ω·cm² (high variability between materials)
- Water-saturated EVA: ~100–1000 Ω·cm² (all materials converge to similar values)
- The resistance collapse occurs because water enables ionic conduction through the polymer matrix
- [[papers/AIP-114-2645-2-s2.0-85071569696-2019-C-Influence of soiling and moisture ingress on long term PID susceptibility of photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=2|Richter et al. (2019), p.2]]

EVA-encapsulated modules reach significant moisture saturation during field aging:

- Initially dry modules (< 0.01% water content) reach saturation (~0.2% water content) within **500–2000 hours** of 85°C/85% RH damp-heat exposure (equivalent to 1–3 years of tropical field conditions)
- PID-free modules in initial dry state develop pronounced PID susceptibility after damp-heat soaking, with shunt conductance increasing proportionally with soaking duration
- [[papers/AIP-114-2645-2-s2.0-85071569696-2019-C-Influence of soiling and moisture ingress on long term PID susceptibility of photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=1|Richter et al. (2019), p.1]]

Moisture dramatically accelerates Na⁺ leaching from soda-lime glass:

- Na concentrations in EVA at the glass interface increase with temperature above 55°C in the presence of moisture
- At 85% RH vs. 25% RH, Na concentrations in EVA were **two orders of magnitude higher** ($\sim 10^2\times$)
- Na concentrations increase exponentially with temperature: **0.422 ppm at 25°C** rising to **4.573 ppm at 75–85°C**
- [[papers/Wiley-286-871-2-s2.0-85183870882-2024-J-Prevention of potential-induced degradation using a moisture barrier in crystalline silicon photovol.pdf#page=2|Alnuaimi et al. (2024), p.2]]

Surface soiling lowers the humidity threshold at which conductive water films form:

- Arizona Test Dust at 20% surface coverage enables capillary condensation at moderate humidity (60–85% RH), forming conductive water films at lower humidity levels than clean glass requires
- This "boosted areal grounding" of the glass surface promotes PID of the **whole module area** rather than just edge regions
- [[papers/AIP-114-2645-2-s2.0-85071569696-2019-C-Influence of soiling and moisture ingress on long term PID susceptibility of photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=3|Richter et al. (2019), p.3]]

The rate of moisture ingress, and thus PID susceptibility, depends strongly on encapsulant and backsheet material choice:

- **EVA volumetric resistance:** $10^{13}$–$10^{14}$ Ω·cm (more susceptible to moisture-enhanced conduction)
- **POE volumetric resistance:** $10^{15}$–$10^{16}$ Ω·cm (water solubility 1 g/m³/mbar; far more resistant)
- POE encapsulant achieves near **0% Pmax degradation** across all backsheet types under PID testing, even when the backsheet allows some moisture ingress
- [[papers/Elsevier-242-1379-2-s2.0-85147101243-2023-J-Impact of different backsheets and encapsulant types on potential induced degradation (PID) of silic.pdf#page=4|Mahmood & TamizhMani (2023), p.4]]

A PTFE moisture barrier reduces Na⁺ penetration into EVA by approximately half at the glass/EVA interface:
- WVTR improved by **29.3%** with PTFE coating; Na concentration in EVA approximately halved
- [[papers/Wiley-286-871-2-s2.0-85183870882-2024-J-Prevention of potential-induced degradation using a moisture barrier in crystalline silicon photovol.pdf#page=3|Alnuaimi et al. (2024), p.3]]

In silicon heterojunction (HJT) modules, damp heat alone (without applied bias) causes **20% loss in Isc** after 500 hours via water-induced glass corrosion creating NaOH molecules, which then attack the TCO layer:
- [[papers/Wiley-251-3004-2-s2.0-85045834850-2018-J-Comprehensive study of potential-induced degradation in silicon heterojunction photovoltaic cell mod.pdf#page=2|Zu et al. (2018), p.2]]
